topic: What if you could see one minute ahead?
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
SEE ONE MINUTE AHEAD?

power.rule: exactly one minute ahead, always on, you can watch but never change it
power.look: the future plays as luminous cyan ghosts while a chip reads AHEAD and a dial counts down the watched minute from +60.00

script.text: Your mug tips — a minute ahead. You slide it back. Saved.
A paper ball's coming. A minute ahead. Duck. Nothing.
A minute ahead, you're down there. You don't move. You go anyway.
What if you could see one minute ahead?

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: One catch: you watch. You can't change a thing. The minute ahead has no light to send. That's real.
So who's playing you the future?

science.claim: The minute ahead has no light to send: every picture your eyes receive was already emitted in the past — the Sun's is over eight minutes old.
science.working: Seeing is receiving light. From the Sun: 1 astronomical unit = 149,597,870,700 m (exact, IAU 2012); c = 299,792,458 m/s (exact by definition); 1.4959787e11 / 2.99792458e8 = 499.0 s = 8 min 19 s at mean distance, 490.6 s = 8 min 11 s at perihelion (1.4710e11 m) — always over eight minutes. Even a wall 3 m away is 10 ns old (3 / 3e8). An image of a future event has no source: no photons from it exist yet, so a present-day eye has nothing to receive.
science.source: IAU 2012 Resolution B2 (astronomical unit fixed as 149,597,870,700 m); speed of light exact by definition; light-time geometry

science.claim: A feed of the future would have to be sent to you — light only ever carries what has already happened.
science.working: An eye builds an image only from photons that scattered off an object and arrived. For a photon to arrive from time t + 60 s, something must have emitted it at t. In relativity nothing from the future can be received: the future hasn't happened, so there is no light in it. A working future view therefore needs a sender that isn't following the rules the sun obeys — which is the question the episode ends on.
